design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using a permuted block randomisation scheme with balanced random blocks of 6, 8, or 10 stratified by study site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated using permuted blocks, concealed in sealed opaque envelopes opened only after consent, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mother-infant dyad assignments to study groups in a 1:1 ratio was by a permuted randomisation scheme, using balanced random blocks of 6, 8 or 10. We stratified the randomisation by study site to account for centre population differences. Randomisation was done in May 2016 at The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Allocation assignments were stored in sealed opaque envelopes and mailed via courier to the local study principal investigators. Only after obtaining written informed consent did the local study teams know the allocation assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and research staff could not be blinded given the nature of phone reminders, healthcare providers delivering immunisations were blinded, there were no important deviations from the protocol, and an intention-to-treat approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neither study participants nor research team were blinded. However, the immunisation clinic staff—those who administered and recorded immunisation—were blinded to study group allocations... With the protocol amendment, we defined two study populations for the primary outcome analysis. First, a modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population—defined as all randomised subjects regardless of where immunisation was received or audited—immunisation record books or phone calls.

domain_judgments.rationale: While loss to follow-up was modest for the primary 18-week outcome (8%), it reached 31% for the 12-month outcomes with limited reporting of the breakdown across intervention arms or formal sensitivity analyses addressing missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Five (0.8%) infants died during the follow-up period, 48 (8%) were lost to follow-up for the primary outcome and 184 (31%) for the 12-month outcomes (figure)... We were, however, able to retain 92% of the enrolled population for the primary outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to a hospital strike, the primary outcome assessment required unblinded research assistants to collect maternal self-reports via telephone for a substantial subset of participants, introducing potential recall or reporting bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, the immunisation clinic staff—those who administered and recorded immunisation—were blinded to study group allocations... Study research assistants called each study participant on the telephone and obtained verbal reports—name and date—of when Penta-1, 2 and 3 were received. We assessed the receipt of measles vaccine solely from the immunisation clinic record book.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT02819895) and the reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with the pre-specified protocol objectives.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration number NCT02819895... The primary outcome was the proportion of infants who received the Penta-1, 2 and 3 immunisations (henceforth referred to as Penta-3) at 18 weeks of age... We defined the secondary outcomes as completing Penta-3 and the measles immunisation by 12 months of age and receiving each within 1 week of the recommended time.

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall due to missing outcome data for longer-term 12-month outcomes (31% loss to follow-up) and potential measurement bias arising from reliance on unblinded phone audit verbal reports for the primary outcome following a hospital strike.

design_rationale: The trial allocated participants using a computer-generated randomization scheme.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated randomization scheme was used and investigators were blinded, an apparent sequence irregularity occurred resulting in significant baseline imbalance in monthly income (p < 0.0001) and paternal employment (p = 0.03).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were allocated to either an intervention or usual care group using a computer-generated randomization scheme with the investigators being blind to the allocation. Upon unlocking the database, it was noted that a disproportionate number of participants were randomized into the intervention group during the first month and the usual care group during the second month of the enrollment period.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was delivered as automated SMS reminders with minimal scope for unintended co-interventions, and both ITT and per-protocol analyses were reported with consistent findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both per protocol and intention to treat analyses were done.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was relatively low (15.6% intervention vs 19.3% usual care) and balanced between groups, with ITT analyses accounting for all randomized individuals.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-four patients (7.5%) were lost to follow-up after the first visit and 32 patients (10.0%) after the second visit for a total of 56 patients (17.4%) lost to follow-up during the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Vaccination completion and clinic visit attendance are objective outcomes verified directly through clinic immunization records.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Research nurses collected data at visits 2 and 3, including information regarding family mobile phone use, receipt of SMS reminders, and vaccines given. Immunization records were able to be confirmed for children who returned to either of the two study sites.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (NCT01663636) and all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes are reported transparently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes for this study were the proportion of parents who were sent SMS messages and parental satisfaction with the intervention. Secondary outcomes included completion of the infant immunization series and the rate of completion by visit and by antigen.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns due to potential issues in the randomization process leading to significant baseline demographic imbalances across groups, although outcome measurement, data completeness, and analysis reporting were robust.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial where mother-child pairs were allocated to intervention or control groups using block randomization stratified by health facility location, performed with an automated system.

domain_judgments.rationale: An automated system was used for block randomization with allocation schedules concealed from clinic staff, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Block randomization was used to allocate mother-child pairs to the intervention or control group based on rural, semi-urban, or urban (Korhogo town) health facility location. Randomization was performed using an automated system and randomization schedules were concealed from health facility personnel.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the reminder intervention, participants could not be blinded, but reminders were automatically sent, no unintended deviations were reported, and all randomized mother-child pairs were analyzed according to assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers in the control group were not provided any SMS or voice messages and were instructed to refer to the child's health card for appointment dates, as per the standard of care in Côte d'Ivoire. A mobile web service platform (Ivocarte®, Abidjan) was used to register the mother's mobile phone number and child's visit schedule. SMS and voice messages were then automatically generated and transmitted to recipients at designated times.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data on facility attendance across scheduled visits were recorded and reported for all 1,596 randomized mother-child pairs.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 1596 mother-child pairs were enrolled in the study: 798 in the intervention group and 798 in the control group. ... Attendance records for each visit were transmitted directly from facility staff to study personnel via the Ivocarte® platform. The study outcome measure was attendance at each visit and included children who were brought to the health facility on the scheduled appointment date or any other time during the study period.

domain_judgments.rationale: Facility attendance and vaccination records are objective outcomes, and health providers recording the attendance were blinded to study group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Health providers were blinded to the randomization scheme, which reduced the likelihood of bias in service delivery and data recording. Also, immunization and VAS data were uploaded to the web server in real-time, which enabled more efficient monitoring of each child's progress.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although all scheduled visit attendance outcomes are fully reported, no trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis protocol is cited or available to evaluate potential selective analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study outcome measure was attendance at each visit and included children who were brought to the health facility on the scheduled appointment date or any other time during the study period. We conducted bivariate analyses and created multivariable logistic regression models to assess differences in visit attendance between the intervention and control group.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with automated concealed randomization, blinded healthcare providers recording attendance, and complete follow-up of all randomized participants. However, the lack of a prospective trial registration or published pre-specified statistical analysis plan raises some concerns for selection of the reported result.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 using a computer-generated randomization list with blocks of 6 and sealed opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated and concealed using sealed opaque envelopes opened after consent, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intervention and control group ratio was 1:1; the randomization list was generated through computer assignments with a block of 6 children, allocated in sealed opaque envelopes that were opened at the time of enrollment after informed consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded due to the nature of SMS reminders, an intention-to-treat analysis was performed including all 150 randomized participants per arm, and no major deviations from intended protocol arose due to the experimental context.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study staff administered the baseline questionnaire at the household level; however, the participants could not be blinded due to overt participation and nature of the intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was 96%, missingness was low (4% overall), balanced across reasons, and all 300 randomized participants were accounted for in the ITT analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 18 weeks of life follow-up, 96.0% (288/300) participants gave follow up interview. Six participants shifted from their homes during the study period (1 in the intervention arm and 5 in the control arm), and 6 children died during the study period (4 in the intervention arm and 2 in the control arm).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment relied partially (around 31%) on parental verbal recall without blinding of participants or data collectors, which could introduce some detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We were able to verify that 69.3% of the participant's vaccination status by physically looking at their EPI card; however, rest of the participant's vaccination status was verbally captured as they were not able to retrieve and show the EPI cards to the study team staff.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01859546) and results are reported according to the pre-specified outcomes and analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01859546... The primary outcome was to compare the proportion of children immunized up to date at 18 weeks of age. The secondary outcome was to evaluate the timing of the vaccine received according to the schedule of the EPI.

design_rationale: This is a four-arm cluster-randomised controlled trial where 152 villages were randomly assigned to study groups using constrained randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Clusters were allocated using constrained computer-generated randomization with public selection of allocation sequences, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced across trial arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A constrained randomisation was done with GAUSS Mathematical and Statistical System by one of the study investigators, which randomly generated 1000 allocations that met the following criteria for balance across study arms... At a public randomisation ceremony on Sept 12, 2013, village chiefs determined the final randomisation outcome by picking numbered balls from a cloth sack to select one of these 1000 sequences, then picking labelled (study group) balls to assign the interventions to the chosen allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were unblinded, the intervention was delivered as intended per protocol and analyzed according to assigned group using modified intention-to-treat analysis accounting for clustering.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention and study design, study participants were not masked to their study group allocation... Primary analyses were done with modified intention-to-treat analyses at the participant level so that participants' outcomes were analysed regardless of the degree of exposure to study interventions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 21% of enrolled participants were excluded from primary outcome analysis due to loss to follow-up, outmigration, death, or missing written MCH documentation, with slight differences in attrition across arms and demographic differences between excluded and analyzed participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After accounting for loss to follow-up, which included outmigration and death, and excluding caregivers who verbally reported their child's immunisation history, the primary analytic sample contained 1600 infant-caregiver pairs who completed a 12-month follow-up survey and provided MCH booklet information for immunisation history; 360 (74%) infant–caregiver pairs from 37 villages (control arm), 388 (82%) pairs from 38 villages (SMS only), 446 (79%) pairs from 38 villages (SMS plus 75 KES), and 406 (83%) pairs from 38 villages (SMS plus 200 KES).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed using objective written records from maternal and child health booklets, validated against clinic records, minimizing the risk of measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data for primary and secondary outcomes came from written immunisation records found on the child's MCH booklet at 12-month follow-up visits. As available, MCH records were compared with prospectively collected immunisation records by HFRs. If there were discrepancies between MCH and prospectively-collected data, the health facility immunisation registries were consulted.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and published with a predefined protocol and statistical analysis plan, and reported outcomes conform to the registered plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT01878435... The proportion of fully immunised children (receiving BCG, three doses of polio vaccine, three doses of pentavalent vaccine, and measles vaccine) by 12 months of age constituted the primary outcome and was analysed with log-binomial regression and General Estimating Equations to account for correlation within clusters.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with sound constrained cluster randomization and objective outcome assessment, but has some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to 21% attrition and differential loss across arms.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were assigned to intervention or control groups using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: While sequence generation was random via computer-generated random numbers, there is no description of allocation concealment prior to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At study initiation study participants were assigned by computer generated random numbers to 1 of 2 groups: no short message service reminder and routine health education and those receiving short message service reminders and health education.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding was not feasible given the nature of the SMS intervention, the intervention was automated/delivered as intended, no significant deviations occurred, and analysis was conducted on all randomized participants according to assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the intervention group, the mother or caregivers received the routine health education and also received automatic messages indicating the next appointment date on three occasions. In the non intervention group, the mothers or caregivers received the routine health education and were informed about their next scheduled visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was 100% follow-up for all 304 randomized participants with complete outcome data available for analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the respondents in both intervention and non intervention groups were followed up at 14 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was receipt of scheduled vaccines verified objectively against clinic immunization registers, which is unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The mothers were followed up by phoning them using the mobile numbers provided and also comparing the details provided with those in the clinic immunization registers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial registration (ISRCTN70918594) was retrospective (registered August 2014, while the trial took place in 2013), and no pre-specified statistical analysis protocol was available.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure was receipt of scheduled vaccines at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. The secondary outcome measures were; delay in immunization appointment, age of child when immunized, costs, and willingness to receive SMS.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to the lack of information regarding allocation sequence concealment and the retrospective registration of the clinical trial without an available pre-specified analysis plan.
